solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Prevent small fairy taking it back

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: 'back' tells us the fairy taking 'it' is read from right to left

parts.note: an elf is a small fairy-like creature of folklore

explanation.surface: Someone tries to stop a tiny fairy from reclaiming something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the fairy-plus-it pair to give TIFLE; 'taking' merely joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: To stifle something is to suppress it, so it is a synonym of prevent.

clue.text: Fake diamond becoming country's emblem

parts.note: a sham is something false or fake
rock is slang for a diamond

explanation.surface: A counterfeit gem is taken up as a national symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The shamrock, a three-leaved clover, is the national emblem of Ireland.

clue.text: Disrespectful during solitary meeting with conservationists

parts.note: in can mean during, as in 'in the night'
sole means single or alone
the NT is the National Trust, a British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: Someone is rude in a private meeting with environmentalists.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent behaviour is rude and lacking in respect.

clue.text: Excellence not initially shown by girl

indicators.note: 'not initially shown' says the opening letter of the word for excellence is hidden away

parts.note: class means excellence or quality

explanation.surface: A girl fails to display top quality at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Lass is a mainly Scottish and northern English word for a girl or young woman.

clue.text: Bent fictional detective seen in books by Poe regularly

indicators.note: 'regularly' says to take every other letter of the name Poe, starting with the first
'seen in' says the detective appears inside the books

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, the books of the later Bible
Charlie Chan is the Chinese-American detective in Earl Derr Biggers's novels

explanation.surface: A crooked fictional detective turns up in Edgar Allan Poe's stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' reads as crooked but means an inclination; 'regularly' picks letters from Poe and 'seen in' puts the detective among the books.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent for something is a natural inclination, which is exactly what a penchant is.

clue.text: Going into hiding ain't awfully amusing

indicators.note: 'hiding' says the word for going into conceals the scrambled letters

parts.note: entering means going into

indicators.note: 'awfully' suggests the letters of ain't are mangled

explanation.surface: Going undercover is hilarious, or so someone claims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' scrambles the contraction to TAIN, and 'hiding' tucks that inside the word for going into.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertaining as an adjective means enjoyable and diverting, close to amusing.

clue.text: Risk having list of names raised by honorary university head

parts.note: to chance something is to risk it

indicators.note: in a down clue 'raised' means the list is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a roll is an official list of names, as in a register

explanation.surface: Someone gambles on the head of a university adding their name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns ROLL into LLOR beneath CHANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: In British universities the chancellor is the titular, largely ceremonial head.

clue.text: Risks ignoring duke in French town

indicators.note: 'ignoring' says the duke is left out of the risks

parts.note: dangers are risks

explanation.surface: A duke shrugs off the hazards of a French town.
explanation.definitionFit: Angers is a town on the Loire in western France, former capital of Anjou.

clue.text: Refuse to hold Henry's party

indicators.note: 'to hold' says the rubbish contains the next letter

parts.note: refuse as a noun is rubbish, trash
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Someone declines to host Henry's celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb but is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrash is informal British slang for a lively party.

clue.text: Musician heading off to find help

indicators.note: 'heading off' says the first letter of the musician is cut away

parts.note: a bassist plays the bass guitar or double bass

explanation.surface: A musician sets off in search of help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the B from BASSIST.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to help; here both are nouns, assistance given.

clue.text: More unusual coming from an outsider

definitions.meaning: someone not known or not belonging to the group

explanation.surface: Something odder emerges from somebody who is not part of the group.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranger is both the comparative of odd-sounding strange and a noun for an unfamiliar person.

clue.text: Fail to arrive before a policeman arrests Rex

indicators.note: 'before' puts the first piece ahead of the rest

parts.note: to come is to arrive

indicators.note: 'arrests' says the policeman holds the king's letter

parts.note: a copper is slang for a police officer
R stands for Rex, Latin for king, as in royal signatures

explanation.surface: A policeman nicks Rex before he can show up.
explanation.definitionFit: To come a cropper is a British idiom for a heavy fall or failure.

clue.text: Ear-splitting, not quiet, by small stream

indicators.note: 'not' says the quiet part is to be dropped from the word before it

parts.note: an ear-splitting sound is shrill
SH is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A piercing, noisy sound beside a little brook.
explanation.definitionFit: A rill is a tiny brook or rivulet, a word mostly kept alive by poetry and crosswords.

clue.text: Heard reportedly by eccentric son of king and queen

indicators.note: 'reportedly' signals that the word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: to catch what someone says is to hear it, so heard can be caught
a card is an amusingly odd person
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Gossip about an odd son of the royal couple.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech CAUGHT and COURT sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: In a pack of playing cards the king and queen, with the jack, are the picture or court cards.

clue.text: Oil giant worried over the Italian judicial proceeding

indicators.note: 'worried' suggests the letters are shaken about and rearranged

parts.note: It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: A worried oil company faces an Italian court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Litigation is the process of taking legal action through the courts.

clue.text: Much to take into account before Lincoln tours Louisiana's capital

indicators.note: 'before' puts the first piece ahead of the next

parts.note: to consider something is to take it into account

indicators.note: 'tours' says Lincoln goes all the way round the capital letter

parts.note: Abe Lincoln, the US president

indicators.note: 'capital' here means the initial letter of the state's name

explanation.surface: Lots to weigh up before Abraham Lincoln visits Baton Rouge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like Baton Rouge but means L, which 'tours' places inside ABE.
explanation.definitionFit: Considerable as an adjective means large in amount, as does much.

clue.text: Show off around island in a state of bliss

indicators.note: 'around' says the display goes either side of the island

parts.note: to parade something is to show it off

explanation.surface: Someone flaunts themselves around an island, utterly happy.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is heaven, and by extension any state of perfect happiness.

clue.text: Residential building providing temporary accommodation to house English soldiers

indicators.note: 'to house' says the shelter holds the next pieces

parts.note: a tent is a shelter put up for a short stay
men is a standard crossword word for soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A block of flats offers short-term shelter to English troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a large building divided into flats, often poor housing.

clue.text: Dejected by widespread desolation around South Carolina

indicators.note: 'around' says the scrambled letters surround the state abbreviation
'widespread' suggests the letters of desolation are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: SC is the postal abbreviation for South Carolina

explanation.surface: Someone is downcast by the devastation spread across a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'widespread' rearranges the fodder to DIONSOLATE, and 'around' wraps that about the state's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Disconsolate means unable to be comforted, deeply unhappy, which is what dejected means.

clue.text: A copper breaks graduate's calculator

indicators.note: 'breaks' says the metal splits the graduate's letters apart

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate, so the graduate's is BA's
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman smashes a student's pocket calculator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads on rods used for doing arithmetic.

clue.text: Look into harsh criticism of one type of race

indicators.note: 'into' says the exclamation goes inside the criticism

parts.note: a slam is a severe criticism
lo is an old exclamation meaning look

explanation.surface: Someone investigates fierce attacks on one kind of race.
explanation.definitionFit: A slalom is a ski or canoe race weaving between gates.

clue.text: Drug free Noel with band taking in LA

indicators.note: 'taking in' says the rearranged letters contain the given pair
'free' suggests the letters of Noel and band are loosened and rearranged

explanation.surface: Noel Gallagher, freed from his band, takes drugs in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges the singer and band to BELDONNA, and 'taking in' slips the city's letters in after the third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Belladonna, deadly nightshade, yields atropine and is used medicinally as a drug.

clue.text: Confront female expert

parts.note: an ace is someone highly skilled

explanation.surface: Take on a skilled woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To face a problem or person is to confront them directly.

clue.text: Make less difficult with each step oddly

parts.note: ea is the commercial abbreviation for each

indicators.note: 'oddly' says to take the odd-numbered letters of step

explanation.surface: Simplify things by working through every odd stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease something is to relieve or simplify it.

clue.text: Muse about everybody that's without work

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
all means every one, everybody

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense of outside: the words for that's sit around work

parts.note: i.e., from Latin id est, means that is
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone ponders everybody who is unemployed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Calliope is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, presiding over epic poetry.

clue.text: Male Carroll character's evil intent

parts.note: Alice is the heroine of Lewis Carroll's Wonderland books

explanation.surface: A male figure from Lewis Carroll harbours wicked plans.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the wish to do harm, a deliberate ill will.

clue.text: Realise shortly before old queen goes around popular theological college

indicators.note: 'before' puts the first piece ahead of the next
'shortly' says the word for realise loses its final letter

parts.note: to see something is to realise it

indicators.note: 'goes around' says the queen's name wraps the word for popular

parts.note: Mary is the name of several past English and Scottish queens
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A sudden realisation before an old queen tours a well-loved college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' docks the last letter of the verb, and 'goes around' has the queen wrap the word for popular.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminary is a college that trains priests or ministers in theology.

clue.text: Become less intense about getting a fast time

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Something eases off on the subject of a quick run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast time' suggests speed, but means a period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to soften or ease off, as when rain relents.
